chunks: We were told by Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: We were told by Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from al-Sa'dan ibn Muslim, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he was asked about jealousy.
He said: It is flesh and blood that circles among people, until it reaches us, and (when it does so) it despairs. That is Shaytan.

key_terms.لَحْمٌ وَدَم: Flesh and blood (metaphor for the spiritual entity)

ai.seo_question: What is the nature of jealousy according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Mani al-Akhbar*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the ontological nature of jealousy (al-hasad) as a tangible spiritual entity composed of flesh and blood that circulates among humanity. He notes that this entity, identified as Shaytan, remains active and influential among people until it reaches the Imams, at which point it despairs of affecting them due to their spiritual immunity. This highlights the unique protective status of the Ahl al-Bayt against the corrupting influence of envy.

en.basel-kadem: 1.	We were told by Muhammed bin Hasan bin Ahmad bin Waleed, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: We were told by Muhammed bin Hasan al-Saffar, from Abbas bin Ma’ruf, from Sa’dan bin Muslim, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, that he was asked about jealousy,
to which he said: It is flesh and blood that circles among people, until it reaches us, and (when it does so) it despairs. That is Shaytan.
